summary: In a 2000 interview Dr. Yehuda Hiss, former head of the Abu Kabir Forensic Institute, admitted that in the 1990s pathologists at the institute harvested organs from Israeli soldiers, Israeli citizens, Palestinians and foreign workers; in 125 cases he and his subordinates removed organs, bones and tissue without family permission, he maintained a “museum of skulls” including IDF soldiers shot in the head, has been investigated for selling organs and falsifying testimony, and was fired as Director after courts became involved but has since remained Chief Pathologist. Hiss said body parts were used by hospitals for transplant purposes — cornea transplants sent to public hospitals — and an Israeli military statement later said the interview facts were accurate and that “this activity ended a decade ago and does not happen any longer.” It remains unconfirmed whether the Swedish newspaper Aftonbladet was correct in alleging Israeli soldiers stole organs from dead and living Palestinians or that Israelis intentionally killed Palestinians for their organs; Aftonbladet alleged soldiers stole organs after killing Palestinians, and Israeli officials have vigorously denied the charges and called the article “anti-semitic.”
